findings.claim: The listed fields (title, description, date) do not say which file each handoff is, so /continue, which loads the handoffs the user picks, has nothing to load them by. The --json shape this plan defines is the contract handoff-and-continue-skills builds on: it needs each entry's path (or concept id) and, with no handoffs folder, an empty list on stdout rather than the 'there are none' sentence.
Each entry now carries concept id and path, and --json prints [] when there are no handoffs, so /continue can load a pick and parse the empty case.

One handoff with bad front matter (YAML that does not parse, or generated that is not a mapping) crashes kmctl handoffs with a traceback, so /continue gets no list at all. The CLI rule says a refusal is one line on stderr naming the file and the fix, and no test covers this path.

as_datetime keeps a non-UTC offset instead of converting it, so its docstring ("an aware UTC datetime") is false, and _date_text labels the local time with Z. generated.at 2026-10-03T09:00:00+02:00 prints as 2026-10-03T09:00:00Z, two hours off.

entries.change: front_matter reads UTF-8 and raises BadFrontMatter naming the file when the YAML or encoding is bad; as_datetime converts an offset datetime to UTC.
live_handoffs skips a handoff with bad front matter and appends a warning naming it, and reads generated.at only when generated is a mapping.
kmctl handoffs prints each skip warning to stderr, so --json output stays one clean list.
Tests for unparseable YAML and a non-mapping generated (skipped with a warning, the rest still listed) and for an offset timestamp shown in UTC.

findings.claim: bad front matter crashed the whole listing
an offset generated.at was printed as if it were UTC
the new astimezone(UTC) call raises OverflowError for a datetime at the edge of the range, such as 0001-01-01T00:00:00+01:00, and the command crashes with a traceback
the not-UTF-8 branch of front_matter has no test; only the bad-YAML and non-mapping generated cases are covered
